text:
kevin: heads-up — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes on text-gen since ~11:02 UTC. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/latency/serving?panel=gen_p99
kevin: p99 up from ~180ms -> ~620ms for redwood-large-1 in us-east-1, p95 also elevated. error budget burn warning fired.
kevin: support ticket IDs: #4492, #4495 (customers on Dedicated + Hosted).
maria: looking now. any deploys around that time? deploy-bot: automated-canary completed at 10:58 UTC.
june: I see an unusual spike in model queue length and consistent CPU throttling on the control-plane proxies at 11:01.
olivia: traces show big slow spans in 'batcher.v2' — KS cache miss rate jumped. suspect cache eviction after an odd churn at ~10:59.
maria: can someone grab a quick top of the serving hosts? kevin — can you run: 
```
ssh ops@serving-1 'sudo tail -n 200 /var/log/serving/proxy.log | grep "batcher" -n'
```
kevin: ran that, snippet: 
```
[11:00:58] batcher: queue_size=1245 delay_ms=430 p99=620
[11:01:03] batcher: cache_miss=true cache_size=0.8GB
[11:01:10] kernel-sched: high-occupancy -> latency spike
```
kevin: also saw a lot of requests hitting long contexts (>4096 tokens) — probably causing larger KV-cache pressure.
maria: ok, immediate mitigations to reduce tail while we investigate: 1) enforce stricter per-API-key concurrency limits, 2) enable circuit-breaker for perpetually slow model variant, 3) route new requests to fallback smaller model and other region if capacity is stressed.
june: agree. I'm going to flip a temporary rate-limit at the edge to protect the backend — patching the gateway config now. Command: 
```
# temp throttle at edge
curl -X POST 'https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/edge-config' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $MGMT' -d '{"global_max_concurrency": 2500, "per_key_max": 50}'
```
deploy-bot: edge-config update started (10:15s)
maria: I'll also change routing policy for 'redwood-large-1' so that traffic to it is limited to 30% and overflow goes to 'redwood-medium-1' and 'redwood-small-1' in us-east-1 and us-west-2.

maria: patching circuit-breaker for the model: 
```
# enable CB for model variant
curl -X POST 'https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/models/redwood-large-1/circuit-breaker' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $MGMT' -d '{"enabled":true, "consecutive_failures":5, "max_in_flight":120, "backoff_ms":5000}'
```

olivia: did that routing change. now observing p99 drop in us-east-1 from 620ms -> 240ms within 90s. p95 almost back to baseline.
kevin: nice. support-bot: can you notify affected customers with an incident note and ETA?
support-bot: note created: Incident #INC-2026 — 'High p99 on text-gen' — customers notified, status: investigating.
june: we still need a durable fix: root cause appears to be a combination of cache churn (large contexts evicting hot prefixes) + an unlucky kernel improvement merged last week that degrades continuous batching under high KV pressure.
maria: file an internal ticket to rollback kernel patch on serving nodes and add a canary gate for that kernel change. june — can you draft the rollback PR?
june: on it. will prep a canary rollout that keeps batcher v1 behavior.
kevin: in parallel we should add SLO guardrails to prevent customer-facing regressions: 1) automatic fallback to smaller model when p99 > 2x baseline for 2m, 2) soft circuit-breaker that returns 503 with 'try-later' header when backend queue depth > threshold, 3) global emergency throttle toggle our ops can flip.
maria: agreed. proposal for guardrail config (short): 
```
- fallback_policy: {
    'trigger_window_s': 120,
    'p99_multiplier': 2.0,
    'fallback_models': ['redwood-medium-1','redwood-small-1'],
  }
- soft_cb: {
    'queue_depth_threshold': 1000,
    'response_code': 503,
  }
- emergency_throttle: manual toggle in console + API
```

olivia: will add those to the SRE playbooks and console controls. also adding a metric export so we break down p99 by model variant + seq_len buckets.
maria: follow-up actions (assigned):
- kevin: monitor customer tickets + coordinate customer comms (INC-2026)
- june: rollback kernel patch canary and open postmortem draft
- olivia: add fallback guardrail + metric slice dashboards
- maria: create automated test that simulates large-context churn and validates batcher latency

kevin: timeline: mitigations in place ~11:06 UTC, p99 stabilized by 11:08 UTC, continued monitoring.
maria: recommend keeping circuit-breaker enabled and routing caps for the next 24h while we validate the rollback and add tests.
june: will kick off rollback canary in 30m.

olivia: adding runbook snippet for future oncall to follow quickly: 
```
1) check /d/latency/serving p95/p99 by model and seq_len
2) if p99 > 2x baseline -> enable fallback_policy via API
3) apply edge throttle: per_key_max = min(50, current_per_key)
4) enable model circuit-breaker (max_in_flight=120)
5) notify customers + start postmortem
```

kevin: thanks all. I'll update INC-2026 with these mitigation steps and close when we're stable.
maria: good job triaging. logging action items in tickets and keeping SLO guardrails as prod priority. :white_check_mark:
